title: Bound RSE data preservation against real GP8 consumers
scope: Separate serializable RSE configuration from proprietary synthesis and unsupported legacy records.
acceptance: Inventory non-default master and track RSE descendants currently covered by parent omission reports.
Find supported GPIF destinations and consumer evidence for each proposed preserved slice.
Produce bounded follow-ups for supported data; retain explicit target limitations for the remainder without claiming audio synthesis parity.

reproduction.instructions: Inventory non-default master and track RSE descendants currently covered by parent omission reports.

evidence.detail: Existing scoped evidence; not proof of all AlphaTab variants.
needs-evidence: Detailed proprietary RSE semantics have no independent retaining target oracle. Opaque archive preservation would be a different contract.

Enumerate the non-default legacy master/track RSE values covered by the existing parent omission reports and verify the exact strict-policy behavior for those descendants. Identify a retaining independent GP8 oracle before proposing semantic effect/synthesizer preservation. Ordinary MIDI/channel-strip and TrackSound fields are separately owned and do not prove RSE equivalence. Record the current oracle boundary if none exists. If opaque archive-member retention is desired, define a separate byte-preservation contract; it must not be presented as public RSE semantic support.
